newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: UK's CDC plans Ivory Coast venture capital fund.
newsitem.headline: UK's CDC plans Ivory Coast venture capital fund.

text.p: Britain's Commonwealth Development Agency plans to set up a venture captial fund in Ivory Coast in 1998 to boost lending for small scale private projects, a CDC manager told Reuters on Friday.

"We are keen on setting up a venture capital fund in Abidjan (commercial capital)," CDC's Ivory Coast director Abou Kone told Reuters. "This would be a venture captial fund for taking shareholdings in existing companies and to allow investments of between 200,000 to two million pounds ($3.3 million) (sterling)," he added.
CDC's normal financing minimum of three million sterling, or a 30 percent shareholding, had cost CDC valuable opportunities in Ivory Coast, the world largest cocoa producer, Kone said.

"I used to systemmatically turn down projects that were small," he said, adding that public sector projects still featured largely in the privatised former British overseas development unit's portfolio.
Private projects would be given more attention in future with a view to taking 10-49 percent shareholdings.

"No more public investment. It has to be private," Kone added. "We are in the process of meeting other investors but it (the fund) should dramatically change our portfolio to over 80 percent private (projects)."

A decision on setting up the fund, which could be in place in the first half of 1998, would be taken after market studies and further reviews of projects' potential cash flows over a ten year investment period, Kone said.
CDC, a finance institution with 24 offices around the world, had already set up venture captial funds in 12 other countries, including Ghana, Tanzania and Kenya, he added.

It wound down its operations in Ivory Coast around the time of devaluation of the CFA franc in 1994, but has since expanded operations in West Africa and applied for stakes in several Ivorian state firms recently up for privatisation.

The privatised former British state development unit in 1996 had 42.4 million sterling invested in Ivory Coast in 1996 against 485 million for the whole of sub-saharan Africa, led by Zambia with 67.6 million.
